subject.title: [Bug]: Embedded runner "Network connection lost" when LLM generates a tool call with large parameters (param generation latency > underlying request timeout)

question: For OpenRouter-routed Anthropic models that remain silent while generating large tool-call arguments, should OpenClaw change default timeout behavior, add provider-specific streaming or argument handling, or keep the current default and rely on explicit provider timeout configuration?
rationale: The fix trades off default stall detection latency, provider-specific behavior, and existing timeout configuration semantics, so source inspection alone cannot choose the durable product policy.

options.title: Prove and fix the provider path
options.body: Run a live OpenRouter Anthropic reproduction and implement the narrowest provider/runtime fix, such as provider activity/tool-argument streaming or timeout handling that preserves normal idle failure detection.

options.title: Document explicit timeout configuration
options.body: Keep current defaults and treat `models.providers.openrouter.timeoutSeconds` as the supported workaround for long silent generations.

options.title: Relax the cloud idle default
options.body: Increase or disable the default cloud idle watchdog for this class of model stream, accepting slower detection of genuinely stalled requests.

recommendation.title: Prove and fix the provider path
recommendation.body: Run a live OpenRouter Anthropic reproduction and implement the narrowest provider/runtime fix, such as provider activity/tool-argument streaming or timeout handling that preserves normal idle failure detection.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant current timeout policy and embedded runner history points to this owner for the product-policy decision.
